dispositions.rationale: Each HTTP response stream owns one request cancellation. Real Labby must cancel an admitted upstream operation on disconnect without cancelling another admitted request.
Labby exposes an HTTP MCP endpoint and must reject a present invalid Origin before dispatch.
Labby receives protocol version metadata mirrored in HTTP headers; disagreement must produce HTTP 400 and JSON-RPC HeaderMismatch (-32020).
Unknown RPC methods at Labby's HTTP MCP endpoint must produce HTTP 404 with JSON-RPC -32601, not an HTML router error or a successful result.

Labby's hosted HTTP request path supports only 2026-07-28, so it must reject a current-version request missing MCP-Protocol-Version before dispatch. Legacy direct-stdio initialization and outbound fallback are separate transport-edge compatibility paths.
Labby must identify an unsupported requested version with the typed negotiation error and supported versions before dispatch.

Labby's hosted HTTP request path supports only 2026-07-28, so older-client GET and DELETE traffic to that endpoint must return 405. Legacy direct-stdio initialization and outbound fallback do not add legacy HTTP streams.

Labby's hosted HTTP request path supports only 2026-07-28 and is stateless, so it must ignore an older client's Mcp-Session-Id header without minting or echoing a session ID. Legacy direct-stdio initialization and outbound fallback are separate compatibility paths.

Labby's hosted HTTP request path supports only 2026-07-28. Product-wire checks prove Last-Event-ID leaves bounded JSON responses unchanged, POST subscriptions/listen starts a fresh SSE stream without event IDs, and the legacy GET resume path returns 405 with Allow: POST. This covers both configured response modes and proves streams are not resumable.
